newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW-Kepco confident of Manila deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Kepco confident of Manila deal.

text.p: Korea Electric Power Corp (Kepco), which posted the lowest bid to construct the largest power plant in the Philippines, said on Friday it expects to be awarded the final contract soon.

John Heegong Hahm, president of Kepco Philippines Corp, the local arm of Kepco, told Reuters the company was looking to invite joint venture partners once the contract for the 1,200 megawatt gas-fired plant was awarded.
"The bidding process was fair, outstanding. So, we hope to start negotiations for the contract soon and finish early," Hahm said in an interview.

"Once negotiations are successful and we are awarded the contract, we are considering taking in equity partners who can take up as much as 49 percent," he said, adding that Kepco will maintain a 51 percent participating interest in the project.
Hahm said companies from the United States, Japan, Singapore and South Korea had sent out feelers for a partnership for the project, but declined to name them.

"We are not yet talking with anybody until negotiations with Napocor (National Power Corp) are over and until we are awarded the contract. We would like to keep quiet on the matter as courtesy to the Philippine government."

State-run National Power Corp (Napocor) announced earlier this week that Kepco was the lowest bidder among five other groups including Hong Kong-based Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (Cepa), which had earlier opposed the rebidding of the project.

Cepa was the lowest bidder during the original bidding held last year but the government decided against awarding it the contract, saying it was using technology provided by Westinghouse Electric Corp.
Westinghouse was, at the time, banned from Philippine government contracts because of a dispute over a separate deal. The ban on Westinghouse has since been revoked.
But Napocor officials were confident the award of the contract to Kepco would go smoothly.

"We were involved with them in negotiations for the rehabilitation of Malaya plant. In a sense, it was a more difficult process because it involved questions regarding the security of tenure of people, but we got through it," said a top Napocor official, speaking anonymously.
Kepco was awarded last year the rehabilitate-operate-manage (ROM) contract for Napocor's existing 650 megawatt Malaya oil-fired power plant in Rizal, east of the capital.
Under the contract, Kepco takes over the plant's operations for a 15-year period.
Napocor sources said other bidders, including Cepa, had accepted Kepco's announcement as the lowest bidder.
"The bidding was done very fairly. I think they did a good job," Edgardo Bautista, executive director at Cepa told Reuters.
In previous bidding procedures, both the technical and financial bids were opened simultaneously and the lowest bidder was announced immediately.
But this time, Napocor opened the technical proposals first in October, studied the bids for two months and then opened the financial bids two weeks ago.
Napocor expects to sign the 25-year build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract for the 1,200 megawatt project in September 1997. Commercial operation of the plant is slated for the year 2002.
